Report_ID: MENQoL sexual subscore absolute change from baseline to week 12
Title: Micro-dose transdermal estradiol for relief of hot flushes in postmenopausal Asian women: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Haines et al.
Comment: Change-from-baseline scores were used because end-of-treatment absolute MENQoL sexual scores were not reported. The extracted means are the paper's verbatim values. MENQoL is worse-is-higher, so both change means must be sign-reversed for synthesis (estradiol +1.0; placebo +0.8) before calculating an SMD such that positive values favor estrogen. The Results state that MENQoL scores were not significantly different but provide no exact p value or test statistic. The analysis used the FAS (80 per arm); outcome-specific nonmissing Ns were not separately reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Micro-dose transdermal 17β-estradiol (E2) 0.014 mg/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Outcome variable: MENQoL sexual subscore absolute change from baseline to week 12
effect_direction: After reversing the worse-is-higher MENQoL scale, SMD > 0 favors estrogen

Title: Comparison between vaginal royal jelly and vaginal estrogen effects on quality of life and vaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women: a clinical trial study
Author: Seyyedi et al.
Comment: Change scores, not end-of-treatment values, were reported and extracted for both arms. MENQOL is worse-is-higher (“Higher scores indicating worse quality of life”), so meta-analysis must reverse direction: the extracted changes correspond to oriented improvement means of +0.81 for lubricant and +4.83 for Premarin, with SDs unchanged. Raw verbatim means are retained in the numeric fields to comply with the anti-hallucination requirement. The pairwise Premarin-versus-lubricant p-value is 0.001; the Table 3 value <0.001 is the three-group omnibus p-value. Table 4 appears misaligned/corrupted and was not used for means or SDs.
Design Type: Double-blind, three-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled clinical trial
domain: Menopause; sexual function and quality of life
Study Environment: Gynecology and obstetrics clinics of Hajar Hospital, Shahrekord University of Medical Sciences
Topic of Content: Vaginal estrogen treatment for menopausal symptoms
Participant type: Married naturally postmenopausal women with vaginal atrophy symptoms
additional_group_ns: Vaginal royal jelly cream 15%: n=24 analyzed (ineligible comparator/intervention for this synthesis)
effect_direction: After reversing the worse-is-higher MENQOL scale, SMD > 0 favors estrogen

Title: Effects of vaginal estradiol tablets and moisturizer on menopause-specific quality of life and mood in healthy postmenopausal women with vaginal symptoms: a randomized clinical trial
Author: Susan J. Diem et al.
Comment: The publication reports change-score means with 95% CIs but does not report SDs of change (or explicitly labeled arm-level SEs). Therefore Hedges' g cannot be calculated from this report under the prespecified mean/SD/n method. Do not treat the reported confidence intervals as SDs. MENQOL is explicitly worse-is-higher (1=best, 8=extremely bothered); for higher-is-better synthesis, reverse the signs of both arm means and the treatment contrast. The extracted reported contrast is -0.4 in the paper's original direction, which corresponds directionally to improvement with estradiol. The moisturizer arm was excluded.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Vaginal estradiol 10 mcg tablet + placebo vaginal gel') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm parallel clinical trial with repeated measures
domain: Postmenopausal sexual function and menopause-specific quality of life
Study Environment: Kaiser Permanente Washington Health Research Institute, Seattle, and University of Minnesota, Minneapolis
Topic of Content: Sexual-function-related bother, including decreased sexual desire, vaginal dryness during intercourse, and avoiding intimacy
Participant type: Postmenopausal women aged 45 to 70 years with moderate-severe vulvovaginal symptoms

Comment: No placebo was used; the eligible comparator was no estriol treatment, with both groups receiving TOT surgery. Final completer sample sizes (36 and 44) were used. Title: Effects of vaginal administration of conjugated estrogens tablet on sexual function in postmenopausal women with sexual dysfunction: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Bumphenkiatikul et al.
Comment: Serious intervention-identity concern: although the trial labels Estromon 0.625 mg as a conjugated-estrogens tablet, the Discussion states that Estromon is a combination of Cynanchum wilfordii Hemsley, Phlomis umbrosa Turczaninow, and Angelica gigas Nakai extracts (CPAE). Eligibility as pharmacologic estrogen alone should therefore be verified before meta-analysis. The abstract also reverses arm sizes; the Results and Table 3 consistently give n=34 for intervention and n=33 for placebo.
